matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Compute the decimal values of both sides of the equation (including any operators). Determine the numeric imbalance and identify a single‑stick transformation that can adjust the values by exactly that amount.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is numerically false and you need to decide which stick move could balance the sides.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick without first checking the numeric difference, leading to a change that doesn't correct the imbalance.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must increase contains a V and the numeric imbalance is exactly +5, reposition one of the V’s diagonal sticks so that it crosses the other stick, turning the V into an X (adding 5).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase a side by exactly 5 and a V is present on that side.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a V to create an X but also altering another numeral, resulting in an invalid equation.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that already has at least one I to another numeral that can accept an additional I (e.g., turning I into II, or II into III) while keeping all numerals valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance can be corrected by adding or removing a single I on either side of the equation.
matchstick.example: Moving an I‑stick from a numeral that would become invalid (e.g., removing the only I from a solitary I) leading to an invalid equation.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must decrease contains an X and the numeric imbalance is exactly –5, reposition one of the X’s diagonal sticks so that it no longer crosses, turning the X into a V (subtracting 5).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to reduce a side by exactly 5 and an X is present on that side.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from an X and placing it elsewhere, leaving the X invalid.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) appear, you can move one horizontal stick from the equals sign to the minus sign, turning the equals into a minus and the minus into an equals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '-' and '=', and swapping them can help balance the numeric values.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' to '-' but leaving '=' with no horizontals, making it invalid.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Remove the vertical stick from a plus sign; the remaining horizontal becomes a minus sign, changing addition to subtraction.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a '+' to '-' to adjust the arithmetic, and the side's numeric imbalance matches the effect.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' but forgetting that the resulting '-' may change the arithmetic incorrectly.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When relocating a stick from the equality sign, ensure at least one horizontal stick remains so that the sign stays a valid '=' (or becomes a valid '-' if appropriate).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you move a stick from the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Moving both horizontals from '=', leaving no operator, resulting in an invalid equation.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality when imbalance is 2
matchstick.principle: If the numeric difference between the two sides is exactly 2, move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the larger side to a numeral on the smaller side, adjusting both sides appropriately.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and an I‑stick can be transferred across the equality sign without breaking numeral validity.
matchstick.example: Transferring an I‑stick across the equality but creating a numeral with too many I's (e.g., IIII).

matchstick.title: Convert '-' to '=' by moving a vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Place a vertical stick onto a minus sign and rotate it to horizontal; the minus gains a second horizontal, becoming an equals sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to turn a '-' into '=', and you have a spare vertical stick that can be repurposed.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to '-' but forgetting to rotate it, resulting in an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '=' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Rotate the vertical stick of a plus sign to become a horizontal and place it on the same sign; the plus becomes an equals sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change '+' to '=', and the vertical stick can be repurposed as a horizontal.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' but leaving the plus without a vertical, making it a '-' instead of '='.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any numeral can donate a stick, ignoring the minimal stick requirements for valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before moving a stick, verify that the source numeral will remain a valid Roman numeral after losing the stick.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the move but neglects to check the resulting equation for syntactic and numeric validity.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After the move, recompute the numeric values and ensure all symbols are valid Roman numerals and operators.

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may stop after making a plausible-looking change without confirming the arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always calculate the values of both sides after the move to confirm equality.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes attempts to adjust multiple symbols simultaneously.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Restrict the transformation to a single stick relocation; track the stick count before and after.

matchstick.description: Creating a non‑canonical Roman numeral (e.g., duplicate V, duplicate L, duplicate D, or more than three I's in a row)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may combine sticks to form numerals that violate standard Roman numeral conventions.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After the move, ensure each numeral follows canonical Roman numeral rules.
